steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Corporate social responsibility (CSR) means businesses consider their impact on society and the environment, not just profit.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Ethical issues include: fair pay and working conditions, avoiding sweatshops, honest advertising, paying fair taxes, and sourcing materials responsibly.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Environmental considerations include: reducing carbon footprint, recycling, sustainable sourcing, minimising waste, and complying with environmental laws.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Pressure groups can influence business behaviour through campaigns, boycotts, and negative publicity - e.g. Greenpeace targeting companies with poor environmental records.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain what is meant by corporate social responsibility and give two examples of how a business might demonstrate it. | Analyse how pressure groups can influence a business's decisions. | Evaluate whether a clothing retailer should switch to using only fair trade cotton, even though it will increase costs by 15%.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always consider the trade-off between ethical behaviour and profit - this is central to AQA questions. Use specific examples when discussing ethics: fair trade, living wage, sustainable sourcing, not just vague statements. Link ethics to competitiveness: ethical businesses may attract customers and staff, improving long-term performance.
